text:
marta: Heads-up — deploybot auto-applied a sticky pin on runtime-3.2 for a subset of models after some OOM spikes. We should agree a decay/unpin plan before the night window.

deploybot: [automated] sticky pin applied. pin_id=pb-2024-11-07-19. Affected: model-group 'q4-late' (llama3-q, gptx-lite). Trigger: kernel crash rate > 3% (5m). See /pins/pb-2024-11-07-19 for metadata.

raj: ok. Who owns the unpin/rollback window? If we unpin bluntly some dedicated pools may see perf variance.

elaine: I can own the nightshift unpin 00:30-01:30 UTC. Prefer canary in eu-west first.

kyle: telemetry indicates mem pressure mostly on longseqs (>8k). Can we do a scoped unpin that only affects shortseq traffic?

marta: I like scoped-unpin. Ops: can we add a pin-decay policy (sticky -> auto-decay after 6h if crash rate falls below threshold)?

ops-sre-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pinning. Suggested command for scoped unpin: `deploybot unpin --pin pb-2024-11-07-19 --scope region:eu-west --traffic-filter 'max_seq<=4096'`. Monitor metrics: `crash_rate`, `p95_latency`, `mem_rss`.

raj: +1 scoped unpin. Also we need release notes updated: note the sticky pin and the targeted unpin plan. @elaine please add to release tracker.

elaine: on it. Drafting rollback criteria: crash_rate <= 1% for 30m AND p95 latency delta < 5% (vs baseline).

marta: proposed schedule: canary scoped-unpin 00:30 UTC -> monitor 30m -> canary decision at 01:00 -> if green roll forward 01:15 -> full unwind 02:00. fallback: re-pin to runtime-3.2 or route to runtime-3.1 if degradation.

kyle: add observability hooks: create temporary alert `pin_decay_rollback_needed` if crash_rate rises >1% after unpin. I'll add dashboards.

deploybot: I can execute the scheduled scoped unpin at 00:30 UTC if this channel acknowledges. React with :eyes: to approve.

raj: ack. :thumbsup:

elaine: approved. I'll be on call and will run the canary checks.

marta: quick blurb for release notes: "Runtime 3.2 temporary sticky pin applied due to memory regression on long sequences. Scoped unpin planned during night window; see internal runbook for details."

ops-sre-bot: Ops checklist:
1) tag canary hosts `pin_canary=pb-2024-11-07-19`
2) execute: `deploybot unpin --pin pb-2024-11-07-19 --scope region:eu-west --traffic-filter 'max_seq<=4096'`
3) watch metrics for 30m (`crash_rate`, `p95_latency`, `mem_rss`)
4) if criteria fail -> rollback: `deploybot pin --pin pb-2024-11-07-19 --force` and notify channel.

marta: pasting helpful commands for on-call ops (manual fallback):
```bash
# inspect pin
deploybot list-pins | jq '.[] | select(.pin_id=="pb-2024-11-07-19")'

# scoped unpin (canary)
deploybot unpin --pin pb-2024-11-07-19 --scope region:eu-west --traffic-filter 'max_seq<=4096'

# rollback (re-pin)
deploybot pin --pin pb-2024-11-07-19 --force
```

kyle: I'll prepare a short eval suite to run against canary hosts to sanity-check model responses and latencies after unpin.

elaine: I'll also update the release tracker and DM the top dedicated customers who might be impacted by runtime changes.

marta: thanks everyone. If anything changes we update this thread. Closing the planning chatter until canary starts.
